findings.explanation: name ("main"), location ("europe-west2-a"), tier ("BASIC_HDD"), file_shares.name ("share1") and file_shares.capacity_gb (1024) are all literals. Only kms_key_name and network_id are parameterized. This means: (1) a consumer cannot deploy the module twice in the same project without a name collision, since name is fixed; (2) every consumer is forced into the same region/zone, tier, and 1TB share size regardless of their actual requirements. For a published, reusable module this is the difference between a module and a single hardcoded resource block.
findings.remediation: Add variables for name, location, tier, file_share name and capacity_gb (with defaults matching current values to stay backward compatible with example/examplea), and wire them into the resource.
findings.title: Core instance attributes are hardcoded, not exposed as variables

findings.explanation: deletion_protection_enabled is not set, so it defaults to false. Filestore is stateful NFS storage; an accidental `terraform destroy`, a bad plan applied against the wrong workspace, or a name/location change that forces replacement will delete the instance and its data with no guardrail.
findings.remediation: Set deletion_protection_enabled = true by default (expose as a variable so callers can opt out for ephemeral/test environments), and add deletion_protection_reason for clarity.
findings.title: Filestore instance has no deletion protection

findings.explanation: BASIC_HDD is a single-zone tier with no built-in failover; GCP's ENTERPRISE tier supports regional replication for HA. Because tier is a literal, no consumer of this module can provision an HA-capable instance without forking the module.
findings.remediation: Expose tier as a variable (default "BASIC_HDD" to preserve current behavior) so production consumers can select ENTERPRISE/regional configurations.
findings.title: Tier is hardcoded to BASIC_HDD with no way to opt into a regional/HA tier

findings.explanation: google_filestore_instance supports description and labels arguments; neither is set on the resource itself (only provider-level default_labels apply in the example). Without them, the instance carries no per-deployment metadata (owner, environment, cost-center) visible in the GCP console.
findings.remediation: Add optional variables for description and labels and pass them through.
findings.title: Resource has no description or labels

suggested_policies.rationale: google_filestore_instance has a deletion_protection_enabled attribute (like google_sql_database_instance and google_compute_instance) but no existing holden policy checks it. The closest existing rule, HLD_GCP_391, is scoped to google_compute_instance only. Filestore is stateful NFS storage with no equivalent of a snapshot-based undo, so an unprotected instance is a one-way door.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_473
name: Filestore instances should enable deletion protection
principle: reliability
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  google_filestore_instance.deletion_protection_enabled defaults to false.
  Without it, an accidental terraform destroy, a plan applied against the
  wrong workspace, or an update that forces replacement deletes the
  instance and its data with no guardrail.
remediation: |
  Set deletion_protection_enabled = true:
    resource "google_filestore_instance" "main" {
      deletion_protection_enabled = true
    }
resources:
  google_filestore_instance:
    path: deletion_protection_enabled
    equals: true
